selected_problem: Fresh main bound GitHub merge requests to the expected validated PR head, but the provider still treated any successful HTTP response whose `merged` field was not explicitly false as a successful merge. A 2xx response with missing merge confirmation could therefore be reported as `mergePerformed=true` and `ok=true` with no immutable merge commit SHA, breaking verifiable and traceable delivery receipts.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: After expected-head binding, one narrow evidence-rich central gap remained at the same remote merge boundary: provider success receipts were not strictly bound to GitHub's explicit merged confirmation plus an immutable merge commit identifier. The committed singular-bottleneck gate routes this replay to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt or fabricated numeric routing score is claimed.

pre_fix_reproduction.method: source-exact focused harness for the pre-fix githubMergePullRequest return contract
pre_fix_reproduction.observed: A mocked HTTP 200 response with `{}` produced `ok=true`, `mergePerformed=true`, `externalSideEffectPerformed=true`, and `sha=null`.
pre_fix_reproduction.consequence: The provider could claim a completed remote merge without explicit GitHub merge confirmation or immutable merge-commit identity.

changes: githubMergePullRequest now accepts success only when GitHub explicitly returns `merged === true`.
A confirmed merge is considered a valid delivery receipt only when GitHub also returns a full 40- or 64-hex merge commit SHA.
Successful HTTP without explicit merge confirmation fails closed with PR_MERGE_NOT_CONFIRMED.

If GitHub explicitly reports a merge but omits or returns a malformed merge SHA, the provider preserves `mergePerformed=true` and `externalSideEffectPerformed=true` while returning `ok=false` with PR_MERGE_SHA_INVALID, so a performed side effect is never falsely erased from the receipt.

cases: HTTP 200 with no explicit `merged=true` fails closed and does not claim a merge side effect
`merged=true` with no immutable merge SHA preserves the performed-side-effect truth while rejecting the delivery receipt
`merged=true` with a full immutable merge SHA succeeds
validation.verification_note: The local verification files were byte-identical to the branch blobs above, confirmed with `git hash-object`. No GitHub Actions were used.

truth_boundaries: This closes false-positive provider merge receipts; it does not make GitHub's merge operation itself transactional with the caller's observation.

The current GitHub merge API still has no caller-supplied expected-base-SHA precondition, so base-branch movement between validation and merge remains a separate unresolved integration-boundary problem.

PR creation remains branch-name based and is not atomically conditioned on an expected remote head SHA; the later merge head precondition prevents silently merging a moved PR head but does not prevent creation of a PR whose head changed before creation.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is introduced.
